To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
assembly-defective OmpCs were isolated and their assembly defects were corrected in a suppressor strain, which is a novel and interesting finding.

(i) the OmpC protein is assembled into a trimeric form in the cytoplasmic membrane, (ii) the OmpF and OmpC proteins are assembled into trimers in the same manner, (iii) OmpC assembly is sensitive to the G-39 and G-224 amino acid residues in the mature OmpC protein, (iv) OmpC and OmpF assembly are sensitive to the G and Q amino acid residues, respectively, in
assembly defects of OmpC proteins can be caused by single-ammino-acid substitutions, by disulfide bonds between nonnative cysteines, or by both.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of OmpC mutants defective in assembly and the isolation and characterization of assembly suppressor alleles.
the identification of assembly-defective OmpCs, the characterization of the assembly defects, and the identification of the asmA3 suppressor allele.
the assembly of OmpC proteins and the mechanism of assembly suppression by asmA3.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
assembly-defective OmpCs were corrected by asmA3 inasmuch as asmA3 was able to suppress the assembly defect by preventing the assembly defect from being expressed.
assembly-defective mutants of OmpC protein can be corrected by asmA3.
the asmA3 suppressive effect is independent of the nature of assembly defect in the mutant OMP protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the asmA3 suppressor corrects the assembly defects of mutant OmpC by a mechanism that is independent of the assembly defect's cause.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the OmpC biogenic pathway is not as robust as previously thought.
the assembly-defective OmpCs are a valuable resource to investigate the mechanism of OmpC assembly in the cell.
the assembly-defective OmpCs can be rescued in two different ways: (i) by preventing the formation of nonnative disulfide bonds and (ii) by suppressing the assembly defect by asmA3.
